test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 28 Jun, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Why are the intermediate goods NOT included in the National Income?

options.text: For the prevention of double accounting.

solution:
The correct answer is __**For the prevention of double accounting.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Intermediate goods** are not included in the National Income to prevent double accounting.
 
• Including intermediate goods would lead to **double counting** because their value is already embedded in the final goods and services.
 
• National Income is a measure of the total value of **final goods and services** produced in an economy over a specific period.
 
• Counting intermediate goods separately would **inflate the National Income** figures inaccurately.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Intermediate goods are those goods that are used as inputs to produce other goods and services.
 
• Examples of intermediate goods include raw materials, components, and parts used in manufacturing.
 
• Final goods are those that are ready for consumption or investment and are included in the calculation of National Income.
 
• To accurately measure the economic activity and avoid overestimation, only the value of final goods and services is counted.
